usage.summary:
I rebuilt the explorer with `Try` and `Abstract`, and the gate passed on the first of the four runs. TLC found 24,762 states at depth 16, and the code reaches the same states at that size and at one size larger. Every witness was reached, every known bug was caught, Gobra proved every contract, and go vet and go test pass. I didn't change the model or any ratified statement.

**The code (`protocol/protocol.go`)**
- The factory's state is now an `Issue` type, built with `NewIssue(questions)`. The number of questions is the only size, and the code keeps no bounds.
- Every operation now decides for itself whether it runs. Where the model's action can't run, it returns `false` and changes nothing. Its Gobra contract states when it runs, what it changes when it does, and that nothing else changes.
- The code decides who may direct it: a person with write access who isn't a bot.
- The code keeps CI's result only for the current head, because that's the only one any action reads. The explorer keeps the results for older heads.

**The explorer (`protocol/explore.go`)**
- The bounds are in their own `const` block, named after the TLA+ constants. `State`, `Init`, `Try`, `Abstract` and `Successors` are all here.
- `Try` tries every step in `Next` with every argument in every state, and reports `s` itself when the code refuses.
- `Successors` keeps the meaning the watcher relies on: only steps the code actually ran.
- I kept every constant the watcher uses, and `protocol_test.go` is unchanged.

**Decisions you may want to check**
- **How actors grow one size larger:** I assumed the gate adds a new value to each of `Actors`, `Writers` and `Bots`. With that assumption, the first `Writers - Bots` actors are the ones who can direct the factory and the last `Bots` actors are bots, which keeps one director at the larger size. The one-size-larger check passed this way.
- **`NoP`, `NoHead` and `NoActor`** are defined in `protocol.go`, outside the bounds block, because they are single values rather than sets.
- **No `"parameters"` entry** was added to `invariant.json`. The only size the code takes is its set of questions, and the instructions say sets need no entry.

pins.name: Spec
pins.says: The factory starts with no post on the issue, and every step is a Next step.

pins.name: TypeOK
pins.says: The issue's state is always one of the ten kinds of post, and everything else the factory knows has its expected type.

pins.name: OnlyDirectorsDirect
pins.says: Every command the factory acted on came from a person with write access, never from anyone else or from a bot.

pins.name: RatifiesCurrentProposal
pins.says: Whenever something is ratified, built or merged, it is the current proposal.

pins.name: NoOpenQuestionsWhenRatified
pins.says: Nothing is ratified while a question is still open.

pins.name: AmendsHeldLock
pins.says: A proposal is ratified only while the base branch holds the lock it amends.

pins.name: MergedGatePassed
pins.says: When the factory merges, CI's gate passed on the commit it merged.

pins.name: MergedCurrentHead
pins.says: When the factory merges, the commit it merged is the pull request's current head.

pins.name: MergedOneProject
pins.says: When the factory merges, the pull request changes only its one project.

pins.name: MergedLockRatified
pins.says: When the factory merges, the project's lock is exactly the ratified proposal.

pins.name: StopLimit
pins.says: At most two builds of an issue stop partway before a writer says retry.

pins.name: StoppedHasNoPullRequest
pins.says: When a build stops, or the factory refuses to start one, there is no pull request.

pins.name: QuestionsAsked
pins.says: The factory can ask questions.

pins.name: GotStuck
pins.says: The factory can get stuck.

pins.name: FoundUnsupported
pins.says: The factory can find an issue unsupported.

pins.name: PullRequestFailed
pins.says: A pull request can fail CI's gate.

pins.name: OthersClosed
pins.says: Someone else can close the pull request.

pins.name: OthersMerged
pins.says: Someone else can merge the pull request.

pins.name: FactoryMerges
pins.says: The factory can merge its pull request.

pins.name: AmendmentMerges
pins.says: The factory can merge an amendment to an existing lock.

pins.name: BuildStopped
pins.says: A build can stop before it makes a pull request, and the factory posts that it failed.

pins.name: BuildRefusedAtLimit
pins.says: After two builds of an issue stop partway, the factory can refuse to start a third and post that the build failed.

pins.name: OwnGateFailed
pins.says: When the code fails the gate in the factory's own run, the factory can open a draft pull request and post that the build failed.

pins.name: CannotMerge
pins.says: A pull request that passed CI's gate but changes more than its one project or has a lock other than the ratified proposal can fail.

pins.name: ObeyAnyone
pins.says: A bot or someone without write access gets the factory to take the issue.

pins.name: RatifyEarlier
pins.says: A ratify naming an earlier proposal's hash is accepted.

pins.name: RatifyOverMovedLock
pins.says: An amendment is ratified after the base branch's lock has moved.

pins.name: MergeOnAnyPass
pins.says: The factory merges a commit that passed CI even though it is no longer the pull request's head.

pins.name: MergeIgnoringLock
pins.says: The factory merges without checking that the project's lock is the ratified proposal.

pins.name: StartPastLimit
pins.says: The factory starts a third build after two builds of the issue have stopped partway and no writer has said retry.

pins.name: MergeFailedBuild
pins.says: The factory merges a pull request whose build failed, before a writer says retry and CI's gate passes.

usage.summary:
I found no problems in `protocol/explore.go`. One design choice needs noting: the explorer keeps the gate results for heads other than the current one itself.

**What I checked**

- **Every step of Next is tried with every argument** (`explore.go:234-275`):
  - For each of the 3 actors: Solve and Revise with every draft, Retry, Choose with every question and every draft, and Ratify with every proposal.
  - Build and BuildFailsGate with every head. StopBuild and RefuseBuild.
  - Push with every head, every lock (NoP included, since `Locks == Proposals \cup {NoP}`) and both scopes.
  - CIGate with pass and with fail. NoticeFail, NoticeUnmergeable, Merge, OthersMerge and OthersClose.
  - BaseMoves with every lock, NoP included. Finished.
  - `drafts()` (`:126-140`) matches the spec's `Drafts`: every non-empty set of questions, one proposal per `p`, plus stuck and unsupported.
  - `actor()` (`:66-69`) gives alice as the only director, mallory without write access, and invbot as a bot that writes. So `Writers \ Bots` is covered, and so are both kinds of non-director.
- **No step is skipped because of the state.** `attempt` has no guards. Every call goes to the code through `do` (`:225-232`), and every refusal is the code's own `false`.
- **Refusals report `s` without reading it back.** That is safe here: every method in `protocol.go` returns `false` before it changes anything (I read all of them, lines 220-754), and their `!ok` postconditions keep every field.
- **States are read back from the code.** `readBack` (`:190-215`) takes every field from the `Issue` the code just changed, including `Open`, `Stops`, `Failure` and `DirectedBy`. `Init()` reads back from `NewIssue`.
- **Parameters.** The code takes one size, `NewIssue(questions)`. That is the size of the set `Questions`, and the explorer passes its `Questions` const, so the manifest's empty parameter list is right. `MaxStops` is fixed at 2 in the spec itself and hard-coded in the code, so it isn't a bound the explorer sets.

**Note: gate results on other heads (`explore.go:202-206`)**

The spec keeps `gate` for every head, but the code keeps only `HeadGate`, the result on the current head. `readBack` updates `Gate[i.Head-1]` from the code and carries the other heads' entries forward from the previous state. When the code reports `Head == NoHead`, it clears them all.

- Each carried entry was read from the code while that head was current.
- Clearing on `NoHead` matches the spec: head becomes NoHead only through `Draft`/`ResetPR`, which resets `gate`.
- Every property that reads `gate` reads it at `mergedHead` or `head`, and both come from the code.

So nothing recorded is invented. It does mean the code can't show a bug that depends on old heads' results, such as `MergeOnAnyPass`, because it holds no such state. The explorer has nothing further to read back.

I didn't read `protocol_test.go`, `ratified.lock` or `request.md`.
